# Same pinned, document-disjoint ranges and equal mixture as the K4/1024 arm.

Selection is the first 1000 source-order documents per corpus eligible for a safe fixed direct K4 prefix. Eligibility uses only deterministic length/structure. The primary arm is one direct K4 merge over 1025–4096 tokens with a direct frozen-teacher target.

The only authorized corpus scan is `[162000,192000)` for each pinned corpus. The stream guard refuses every other interval before importing the corpus loader. The declared contiguous refusal partition covers `[0,162000)`, explicitly including official v5, clean-v6 fresh TRAIN, clean-v6 fresh development, and `[161000,162000)` as a mandatory buffer.

For each of the same four pinned corpora, scan in source order and accept the first 1000 nonblank documents whose deterministic safe prefix contains 1025--4096 teacher tokens. Eligibility uses no model output. Once eligible, a document cannot be skipped, shortened, or replaced after an operational failure. Both arms use the identical accepted source IDs and order.
- Population: first 1000 safe-prefix-length-eligible documents per pinned corpus, same documents in both arms.

The tests cover the exact scan/refusal partition, lazy corpus import, deterministic eligibility, exact tail coverage, direct/full validators, unrestricted deep recursion, every-internal-merge decoder telemetry, grouped fixed attacks, exact 2000-replicate source-group bootstrap, shared three-seed units, all gate components, atomic claims/storage failure, and the sole-target text invariant.
